issueCommentThread.body:
Adoption blocker.

This is about Gates: the check that stands in the doorway before work is called good. A green result should mean Directive actually looked. A red result should say what to do next.

What a new person hits: When a check fails, the message does not tell the agent, or the person, how to fix it.

Why that ruins the product for them: They are stopped, and the stop sign has no instruction. That is where a first session gets abandoned.

How likely: High the first time any check fails, which is likely during a first project.

design-critique: warranted, because Directive has many deterministic gates whose failure output is the agent's only self-correction channel, yet there is no standard requiring agent-actionable remediation (what failed / why / how to fix / where), so opaque gate failures still halt agents without teaching them.

refutation-target: Existing verify:* / lint / check failure messages are already sufficiently agent-actionable in practice, so Directive needs no gate-failure output contract (what failed / why / how to fix / where), no audit of opaque failures as bugs, and no patterns/ mirror for consumer projects.

P3. Opaque failures are not treated as bugs via an audit of directive's own gates (verify:*, encoding, branch-policy, vBRIEF, capacity, forward-coverage, and peers).

## Absolute sufficiency claim fails against named-cause fallbacks
blocks-the-design
Evidence: At the dispatch SHA, `packages/core/src/check/named-cause.ts` `#3282` already formats check failures as `gate` / `cause` / `remedy`, but `GATE_REMEDIES` covers only a minority of `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES` / `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES` ids (22 specific keys; most composition gates hit the generic fallback). Live `formatNamedCauseFailure` against empty stderr for `verify:closing-keywords` and `docs:rule-map:check` produced `cause: gate exited 1 without a diagnostic message` and `remedy: Re-run the gate for details: task <id> …`. The same formatter for `verify:stubs` with cause `stub leftover in foo.ts` still attached only that generic re-run remedy. `formatNamedCauseFailure` call sites are the check orchestrators (`cached-orchestrator.ts` / exports), not every direct `task verify:*` path.
Failure mode: Binding the recorded refutation target as written (“already sufficiently agent-actionable … needs no gate-failure output contract … no audit … no patterns/ mirror”) would close #1883 while the swarm correction channel still often receives only “re-run the gate” or an empty-diagnostic cause. Under the injection / swarm lens, that text is the agent’s only self-correction channel on a red check, so the absolute sufficiency premise does not hold.
Disposition: Do not bind the refutation target verbatim. A successor lean must drop or narrow the “already sufficiently … so need nothing” claim before bind.

## Existing #3282 / #3070 mechanisms are the inventory base
sharpens-framing
Evidence: `named-cause.ts` header states gate failures must report gate name, cause, and remedy (not bare exit 1). `cached-orchestrator.ts` wraps hard and advisory hygiene failures with `formatNamedCauseFailure`, emits degraded skip reports with cause/remedy, and preflights consumer deposits via `formatConsumerGateIntegrityFailure` (`consumer-gate-integrity.ts` `#3070`) instead of opaque go-task “Task does not exist” exits. Per-gate remediation constants already exist (`INTENT_CONSTRAINT_REMEDIATION`, `OBSERVABLE_SCOPE_REMEDIATION`, `EMPTY_AC_REMEDY`, hang-detector / CLI-missing branches). Live `task verify:branch` / `verify:encoding` / `verify:closing-keywords` at this dest exited 0 with clear status lines; closing-keywords core FAIL strings at the SHA already name rewrite / Tracking / `--allow-close` recovery. No `content/coding/*` or `content/patterns/*` file at this SHA defines a gate-failure output contract; `gate-integrity.md` and Fail Loud `#1006` are adjacent different grains.
Failure mode: A lean that either pretends no agent-actionable gate-output machinery exists (issue body / Stop 1 warrant) or that invents a greenfield `coding/`+`tools/`+`patterns/` trilogy without extending `#3282` will mis-scope the harvest: duplicate a landed seam, or erase real residual gaps on that seam.
Disposition: Before bind, inventory `#3282` named-cause + `#3070` integrity as the existing mechanism. Prefer extending `GATE_REMEDIES` / cause extraction / treating empty-diagnostic or generic-only remedies as bugs on that seam over a parallel docs trilogy, unless the lean explicitly scopes consumer custom-lint message guidance as a separate optional grain.

## Road-not-taken
footnote
Evidence: Fork considered after the inventory above: (A) refute by claiming current messages are already enough and refuse all three proposal legs; (B) refute only the greenfield trilogy while keeping `#3282` gap-audit as residual; (C) accept the issue’s coding/tools/patterns package as written.
Failure mode: Choosing (A) without narrowing recreates the blocking finding. Choosing (C) ignores landed `#3282`/`#3070` and risks docs-without-enforcement.
Disposition: Census only. Steelman for (A): many product FAIL strings (e.g. closing-keywords intent/FP modes) are already fix-and-retry quality, and a patterns mirror alone does not improve Directive verify output. What would flip this seat toward sustaining (A) unchanged: measured evidence that agents already recover from generic-remedy / empty-cause check failures without human translation. No such measurement was in envelope through id ceiling `5837329065`.

## Refutation target survival
The recorded refutation target does not survive as written. Absolute “already sufficiently agent-actionable … needs no contract / audit / patterns mirror” is blocked by the `#3282` generic-fallback and empty-diagnostic evidence above. A narrowed refutation that refuses a greenfield coding/tools/patterns trilogy while naming `#3282`/`#3070` as the mechanism to extend, and treating opaque or remedy-free failures on that seam as bugs, could still be the charter path after a successor lean recut.

metadata.issueBody:
## Summary
External signal: OpenAI's [Harness engineering](https://openai.com/index/harness-engineering/) report. A precise, cheap, broadly-applicable practice: **"Because the lints are custom, we write the error messages to inject remediation instructions into agent context."** Reviewed via the `deft-directive-article-review` skill.

## The principle
When a deterministic gate fails, its output is the agent's *only* feedback channel for self-correction. So every gate/lint failure message MUST be **agent-actionable**:
- name the violation,
- name the **remediation** (what to change),
- carry the location (path/line) and, ideally, a machine-parseable structure,

so an agent can fix and retry without a human translating the failure. The article frames this as a force multiplier: "once encoded, they apply everywhere at once."

## Directive status
Directive has many deterministic gates (`verify:*`, encoding, branch-policy, vBRIEF, capacity, forward-coverage). Their failure messages vary in quality, and there is **no standard requiring agent-actionable remediation** in gate output. This is the difference between a gate that halts an agent and a gate that *teaches* it.

## Proposal
- A `coding/` + `tools/` standard: a **gate-failure output contract** — what failed / why / how to fix / where.
- Audit directive's own gates (`scripts/verify_*.py`, lints) for compliance; treat opaque failures as bugs.
- Mirror it as a `patterns/` entry for directive-created projects: custom lint/CI messages carry remediation for the agents that will consume them.

## Consumer-value note
High, cheap, universal — turns every gate into a self-healing loop for agents at any throughput/scale. One of the two broadly-valuable lessons from this article (with the AGENTS.md-as-map issue).

## Related
- #1638 (interface-hygiene rules); #1580 (fact vs judgment labeling); #1310 (forward-coverage gate prose → deterministic).

Source quality: practitioner engineering report (OpenAI, single team), directional — no independent eval.
